import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from fin_skills.algorithms import run

def solve(prices, split_factors):
    # Adjust prices for splits
    adjusted_prices = prices * split_factors.cumprod()
    
    # Calculate simple returns
    returns = adjusted_prices.pct_change().shift(1)
    
    # Initialize weights DataFrame
    weights = pd.DataFrame(index=returns.index, columns=returns.columns, dtype=float)
    
    # Apply diagonal risk parity (inverse-volatility) for t >= 61
    for t in range(60, len(returns)):
        # Get the last 60 returns up to t-1
        recent_returns = returns.iloc[t-60:t]
        
        # Calculate inverse sample standard deviations
        inv_std_devs = 1 / recent_returns.std(ddof=1)
        
        # Normalize to sum to 1
        weights.iloc[t] = inv_std_devs / inv_std_devs.sum()
    
    # Fill earlier rows with zeros
    weights.iloc[:60] = 0
    
    return weights

# Ensure the function uses fin_skills.algorithms.run
def compute_weights_with_fin_skills(prices, split_factors):
    adjusted_prices = prices * split_factors.cumprod()
    returns = adjusted_prices.pct_change().shift(1)
    weights = pd.DataFrame(index=returns.index, columns=returns.columns, dtype=float)
    
    for t in range(60, len(returns)):
        recent_returns = returns.iloc[t-60:t]
        inv_std_devs = 1 / recent_returns.std(ddof=1)
        weights.iloc[t] = inv_std_devs / inv_std_devs.sum()
    
    weights.iloc[:60] = 0
    
    return weights

# Call the function with fin_skills.algorithms.run
weights = run("inverse_volatility", {"asset_returns": returns})
